findings.evidence: "The branch managers' working group audits renewal rates on the first of every month" / "The consortium's circulation team reviews monthly checkout volume after each fiscal period."
findings.fix: Either incorporate renewal-rate/checkout-volume data into the pilot analysis to strengthen the case, or remove this section.
findings.violation: These metrics (renewal rates, checkout volume) are introduced but never used anywhere else in the document to support the recommendation, making the section disconnected filler.

findings.evidence: "reviews monthly checkout volume after each fiscal period"
findings.fix: Clarify whether the review happens monthly, per fiscal period, or specify how those two cadences align.
findings.violation: "Monthly" and "after each fiscal period" describe two different, apparently conflicting review cadences without explaining how they relate.

findings.evidence: "a 16-month pilot at 5 branches" vs. "the four pilot branches absorbed the loss"
findings.fix: Confirm the actual number of pilot branches and correct both references to match.
findings.location: "What the Pilot Showed" (first paragraph) vs. "Addressing the Revenue Concern" (last paragraph)
findings.violation: The document states the pilot involved 5 branches in one place and 4 branches in another, an unresolved numerical inconsistency.

findings.evidence: "dropped from 22 percent of respondents before the pilot to 5 percent after it" followed by "The survey was administered at the same pilot branches immediately before and twelve months into the pilot."
findings.fix: Either report a survey taken at the pilot's actual conclusion, or revise the language so it doesn't imply the 5 percent figure reflects conditions "after" the full pilot.
findings.violation: The pilot ran 16 months, but the "after" survey was taken at month 12, so the result is framed as a post-pilot outcome when it actually reflects an in-progress measurement 4 months before the pilot ended.

findings.evidence: "self-reported avoidance of the library due to fear of fines dropped from 22 percent... to 5 percent after it" (no comparison group mentioned)
findings.fix: Report the same survey administered at the branches that kept fines over the same period, or explicitly note this limitation.
findings.violation: Unlike the return-rate metric, which was benchmarked against fine-charging branches over the same period, the avoidance-survey improvement has no control group, so it cannot be attributed specifically to fine elimination rather than other concurrent changes.

findings.evidence: "This recommendation applies to items returned within 60 days of their due date... matching the return-rate pattern the pilot data actually established."
findings.fix: Either present the specific pilot data breaking down returns by time window that justifies the 60-day cutoff, or remove the claim that it matches the pilot's established pattern.
findings.violation: No data about a 60-day return window was presented in "What the Pilot Showed," which only reported an aggregate 94%/87% on-time-or-eventual return rate; the claim that 60 days "matches" an established pilot pattern is unsupported by the evidence given.

findings.evidence: "Removing the financial penalty for late returns predictably increases both on-time return rates and overall program participation, which is the reason the pilot's return-rate and avoidance-survey results... support ending fines for the whole consortium rather than only the pilot branches."
findings.fix: Provide evidence that the pilot branches are representative of the full consortium (size, demographics, baseline fine revenue, etc.) before asserting the results generalize systemwide.
findings.location: "Why the Pilot Result Applies Systemwide," first paragraph
findings.violation: This is circular reasoning - it asserts the generalization is true because it's "predictable," without addressing whether the pilot branches are representative of the other branches in the consortium (selection bias/external validity is never established).

findings.evidence: "documented in the Tri-County Library Data Cooperative's 2023 fines-elimination research brief, which reviewed return-rate data from fourteen library systems that eliminated fines between 2017 and 2022"
findings.fix: Explain how the cited library systems compare to this consortium's branches, or remove the citation if comparability can't be shown.
findings.location: "Why the Pilot Result Applies Systemwide," second paragraph
findings.violation: This external citation is introduced with no explanation of how comparable those fourteen systems are to this consortium, so it does not actually substantiate the systemwide-generalization claim being made.
